subject: System Design
title: Storage Engines Under the Hood
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Storage Engines Under the Hood.

hook.text: You write data to a database. But how does it actually end up on disk? The storage engine decides.

buildup.text: A storage engine manages how data is written to and read from disk. It's the database's core.

discovery.text: B-tree engines update data in place. LSM-tree engines write sequentially and merge later.

twist.text: B-trees are better for reads. LSM-trees are better for writes. The engine defines the database's personality.

climax.text: Understanding storage engines explains why PostgreSQL and Cassandra behave so differently.

punchline.text: The storage engine is the personality of the database.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between B-tree and LSM-tree engines?
options: B-trees update in place; LSM-trees write sequentially and merge
